long_biography.plain_text:
Art patron Adrian Burr collected with a particular purpose: he and his partner, Peter Tatham, sought major works by established New Zealand artists, often buying on the secondary market. Their selection included Bill Hammond's Living Large No. 7, acquired because they wanted an important example of his bird paintings.

Burr also backed projects beyond collecting. His support for Dane Mitchell's Post Hoc exhibition enabled a documentary to follow its creation in China and New Zealand through to installation in Venice. After serving as an executive producer of The Girl on the Bridge, he helped provide office space for Voices of Hope, supporting its mental-health advocacy.
